questions.q: Which Get Data option loads a pandas DataFrame into Power BI?
options: Get Data -> More... -> Other -> Python script
Get Data -> SQL Server
Get Data -> Excel Workbook
Get Data -> Web
questions.explain: The Python script data source runs an actual Python script and exposes resulting DataFrames as tables.

questions.q: Why does this project's load step differ from the Beginner project's connection?
options: The combined dataset only exists as a DataFrame produced by a Python script, not as a table anywhere in SQL Server
Power BI cannot connect to SQL Server anymore
AdventureWorks2012 no longer exists
Python scripts are always faster than SQL connectors
questions.explain: The Beginner project connected straight to SQL Server; this project's real output is a pandas DataFrame, which needs a different data source type.

questions.q: What does Power Query's Navigator show after a Python script step runs?
options: Every DataFrame left in that script's memory, as a selectable table
Only the final printed line of the script
A list of all CSV files on disk
Nothing, until the script is rewritten in M
questions.explain: All DataFrames present after the script runs (customer_df, territory_df, combined_df) appear as Navigator options.

questions.q: Which DataFrame actually gets loaded into the Power BI model?
options: Only combined_df
All three DataFrames, always
Only customer_df
Only territory_df
questions.explain: customer_df and territory_df were intermediate steps; only the final combined_df is selected and loaded.

questions.q: What does Power BI actually re-run on every refresh with a Python script data source?
options: The entire Python script from the top, including the pd.read_csv() calls
Only the last line of the script
A cached copy of combined_df, never the script itself
A SQL query generated automatically from the script
questions.explain: Every refresh re-executes the whole script -- a detail that matters directly for Lesson 12's gateway discussion.
